questions.q: Meridian's pipeline looked healthy at 3x coverage but the team kept missing quota. What did the days-in-stage report reveal?
options: The quota itself was set too high
A large share of the pipeline had been stuck in Proposal far past the normal cycle time
The report type was missing the Amount field
The sales team had stopped logging new opportunities
questions.explain: Total pipeline value alone didn't show that 40% of it had been stale in Proposal for over 60 days — well past Meridian's typical 21-day cycle. Days-in-stage was the report that exposed it.

questions.q: Why was the support team's 18-hour average resolution time misleading?
options: It was calculated using the wrong object entirely
It blended a large volume of fast, simple cases with a small number of slow, high-impact warranty claims into one number
It only counted cases closed on weekends
Average resolution time cannot be reported on in Salesforce
questions.explain: A single blended average hid the fact that warranty claims — the cases customers actually remembered and rated — were taking 4-5 days, while fast account-admin cases pulled the average down.

questions.q: What report-level change fixed the misleading resolution-time average?
options: Deleting all warranty claim cases from the report
Rebuilding the report as a Matrix grouped by Case Type, to separate fast and slow case categories
Switching the report to Tabular format
Removing the date grouping entirely
questions.explain: Adding Case Type as a grouping split the blended average into distinct, honest numbers for each case category, instead of one misleading overall figure.

questions.q: How did Meridian serve both the VP of Sales and the Director of Support from one dashboard build instead of two?
options: By giving both leaders System Administrator access
By combining both fixed components into a shared folder and using a dynamic dashboard so each leader sees their own team's numbers
By exporting both reports to a shared spreadsheet
By scheduling the dashboard to email both leaders separately
questions.explain: A dynamic dashboard (Lesson 17) run from a shared folder (Lesson 10) let one dashboard definition show each viewer their own relevant data, rather than requiring a separate dashboard per audience.

questions.q: What's the common pattern across both of Meridian's fixes?
options: Both required purchasing additional Salesforce licenses
Both were solved with more specific grouping that exposed what a single total or average was hiding, not by adding new data
Both required switching from Lightning Experience to Salesforce Classic
Both were ultimately data-quality problems, not reporting problems
questions.explain: In both cases, the existing data was sufficient — the problem was that a single total (pipeline value) or a single average (resolution time) was masking the real story. A more specific grouping, not new data, revealed it.
